This is a practical, living reference for neurology residents at the University of Florida, Gainesville.

It is designed to be used at the bedside and on call --- focused on high-yield clinical decision-making, admission orders, treatment algorithms, and common consult questions.

## Purpose

-   Provide rapid access to institutional and evidence-based approaches to common neurologic emergencies and inpatient problems
-   Standardize initial work-ups and management across the residency
-   Serve as a continuously updated resource rather than a static printed handbook

## How to Use

-   Use the **search bar** or browse by section in the navigation
-   Most pages are intentionally concise and action-oriented
-   When institutional preferences or order sets exist, they are reflected here

## Contributing & Feedback

This is a **living document**. Content is expected to evolve with new evidence, changing institutional protocols, and feedback from the department.

-   To suggest edits, corrections, or new content, open an issue or pull request on the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/ufneurology/handbook)
-   You can also use the "Edit" or "Issue" links in the page footer

::: callout-warning
This handbook is intended as a **clinical reference aid** for UF Neurology trainees and faculty.

It does **not** replace clinical judgment, attending supervision, or official institutional policies and order sets.

Drug dosing, contraindications, and local protocols should always be verified. When in doubt, discuss with the appropriate attending or fellow.
:::

## Acknowledgments

Originally adapted from the UF Neurology Resident Handbook (2026--2027) and converted into a modular Quarto website for easier maintenance and continuous updating.
